title: 2 Chronicles 33
paragraphs: ¹ Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. ² He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, following the detestable practices of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites. ³ He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had demolished, erected altars to the Baals, made Asherah poles, and bowed down to all the starry hosts of heaven and worshipped them. ⁴ He built altars in the house of the LORD — the very place where the LORD had said, "My name will remain in Jerusalem forever." ⁵ In both courts of the house of the LORD he built altars for all the heavenly bodies.

⁶ He sacrificed his children in the fire in the Valley of Ben Hinnom. He practiced divination and witchcraft, consulted mediums and spiritists, and did great evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger. ⁷ He took the carved idol he had made and placed it in the house of God — in the very house where God had told David and his son Solomon, "In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, I will establish my name forever. ⁸ I will not again remove the feet of Israel from the land I assigned to your ancestors, if only they take care to do everything I have commanded them — all the law, decrees, and regulations given through Moses." ⁹ But Manasseh led Judah and the people of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites. ¹⁰ The LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they paid no attention.

¹¹ So the LORD brought against them the commanders of the Assyrian army, who captured Manasseh, put a hook through his nose, bound him with bronze chains, and led him away to Babylon. ¹² In his distress, Manasseh sought the favor of the LORD his God and humbled himself deeply before the God of his ancestors. ¹³ He prayed to him, and God was moved by his plea and listened to his prayer, bringing him back to Jerusalem and restoring his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD is God. ¹⁴ Afterward he built an outer wall for the City of David, west of the Gihon Spring in the valley, extending to the entrance of the Fish Gate and encircling the hill of Ophel, which he raised to a great height. He also placed military commanders in all the fortified cities of Judah. ¹⁵ He removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, along with all the altars he had built on the temple hill and in Jerusalem, and he threw them out of the city.

¹⁶ Then he restored the altar of the LORD and sacrificed fellowship offerings and thank offerings on it, and told all of Judah to serve the LORD, the God of Israel. ¹⁷ The people still sacrificed at the high places, but they did so only to the LORD their God. ¹⁸ The rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD, the God of Israel, are recorded in the annals of the kings of Israel. ¹⁹ His prayer and how God was moved by his plea, all his sin and unfaithfulness, and the locations where he built high places and set up Asherah poles and idols before he humbled himself — all of this is recorded in the records of his seers. ²⁰ Manasseh died and was buried in his own palace, and his son Amon reigned in his place.

²¹ Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. ²² He did evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Manasseh had done — Amon offered sacrifices to all the carved idols that Manasseh had made, and he served them. ²³ Unlike his father Manasseh, he did not humble himself before the LORD; instead, Amon increased his guilt. ²⁴ His officials conspired against him and put him to death in his own palace. ²⁵ But the people of the land killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
